lines.text: But leaving aside for the present such traditions, some of the
principal ones of which will have to be noticed in a
suitable place in the sequel, let us first turn to a question
which lies on the very threshold of our inquiry. What is
this work, and who is the real author of it? Writing in
1801, speaking of Bhartṛihari, Colebrooke said: "Whether any
beautiful poems have been composed by him, besides the mor-
al reflections which the poet is supposed to make on the dis-
covery of his wife's infidelity. It consists of either three or four
S'atakas or centuries of couplets."[‡] In this passage,
we cannot but think that the learned writer has been betrayed
into some inaccuracy. In the first place, it is only the sec-
